_strings.@@4ec28ebac62f: Indiana529 Education Savings Plan Credit (credit code 837) — Any Indiana taxpayer who makes a contribution to an Indiana529 (formerly CollegeChoice 529) Education Savings Plan account during the tax year; the taxpayer need not be the account owner. _strings.@@5b57e1024e05: Unified Tax Credit for the Elderly — You and/or your spouse must have been age 65 or older by Dec. 31, 2024; if married and living together at any time during the year you must file a joint return; you must have been an Indiana resident for at least six months during 2024; and you must not have been in prison for 180 days or more in 2024. Disabled persons under age 65 do not qualify. The tax return must be filed and credit claimed within three years of the filing due date (including extensions). _strings.@@668a22487ac1: Lake County (Indiana) Residential Income Tax Credit — Available only to residents who paid property tax to Lake County, Indiana on their residence (principal dwelling, owned or being bought under contract); whose Modified Indiana Adjusted Gross Income is less than $18,600 (less than $9,300 married filing separately); and who are NOT claiming the Homeowner's Residential Property Tax Deduction on Indiana Schedule 2, line 2. _strings.@@a4a8e82ba422: Treaty conformity — IN conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from IN income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the IN return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Indiana's resident return (Form IT-40) starts from federal adjusted gross income: the 2024 Form IT-40 Line 1 is "Enter your federal adjusted gross income from your federal income tax return, Form 1040 or Form 1040-SR, line 11," and the 2024 booklet Line 1 instruction repeats "Enter the adjusted gross income from your federal Form 1040/1040-SR, line 11." Income exempt from federal tax under a U.S. tax treaty is already excluded from federal AGI, so it flows through to Indiana untaxed. The only Indiana additions are Schedule 1: Add-Backs, which are IRC-conformity / decoupling items (the 2024 booklet's What's New adds one new add-back — NOL Reduction Due to Debt Discharge, code 155 — to the existing conformity list; Line 1 of Form IT-40 assumes conformity with the Internal Revenue Code as amended and in effect on Jan. 1, 2023). A full-text search of the entire 2024 IT-40 booklet returns ZERO occurrences of "treaty"/"treaties" — there is no add-back for treaty-exempt or U.S.-tax-treaty income. Because IN starts from federal AGI and has no treaty add-back, federally treaty-exempt income is NOT re-taxed -> conforms. (Contrast with CA, which adds treaty income back on Schedule CA.)

Tax line: IT-40 Line 8: "State adjusted gross income tax: multiply line 7 by 3.05% (.0305)" (Line 7 = Indiana adjusted gross income = Line 5 minus Line 6 exemptions; Line 1 starts from federal AGI, Form 1040/1040-SR line 11). Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): additional_dependent_child ($1,500 — Schedule 3 Line 3: additional $1,500 per qualifying dependent CHILD (son/stepdaughter/foster child/legal-guardian child etc., under 19 by Dec. 31, 2024, or a full-time student under 24). NOT applied by calc.state_tax — enter it on Schedule 3 Line 3.); adopted_child ($3,000 — Schedule 3 Line 6: additional $3,000 per adopted child listed on Schedule IN-DEP-A. NOT applied by calc.state_tax.); age_65_low_income ($500 — Schedule 3 Line 5: additional $500 per 65-or-older box when IT-40 Line 1 (federal AGI) is under $40,000 (under $20,000 married filing separately). NOT applied by calc.state_tax.); age_65_or_blind ($1,000 — Schedule 3 Line 4: $1,000 per 65-or-older / blind checkbox (taxpayer and spouse each). NOT applied by calc.state_tax.) This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: First-year $3,000 dependent-child amount (instead of $1,500) has NARROWER mechanics than "first year claimed" — per the 2024 IT-40 booklet it is allowed only in "the first taxable year in which the additional dependent exemption is allowable for that child" and "is not permitted if the child could have been claimed for the $1,500 exemption in any previous year, regardless of whether the child had been claimed." Eligibility gates on could-have-claimed, not first-actually-claimed — decide it on Schedule 3/Schedule IN-DEP, not here. Indiana COUNTY income taxes (IT-40 Line 9, Schedule CT-40, per-county rates) are NOT modeled — calc.state_tax computes the state 3.05% line only; most Indiana filers also owe a county add-on. Rate is year-specific: 3.05% applies to tax year 2024 only (2023 was 3.15%) — never carry either rate to another year.
